question: Can denoising and contractive autoencoders be reformulated intrinsically on known Riemannian data spaces so that their reconstruction displacement estimates the manifold score without coordinate artifacts?

key_findings.claim: The paper replaces each Euclidean autoencoder ingredient with a geometric counterpart rather than changing only the network architecture.
key_findings.evidence: Reconstruction uses squared geodesic distance, denoising noise is sampled isotropically in the tangent space and mapped through the exponential map, and contraction uses the harmonic-map Dirichlet energy Tr(J^T H J G^-1). These quantities remain invariant under local-coordinate changes.

key_findings.claim: For both the geometric denoising autoencoder and geometric reconstruction-contractive autoencoder, the small-noise reconstruction residual estimates the Riemannian log-density gradient.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 derives d log rho_g/dx = G(x)(r(x)-x)/sigma^2 + O(sigma^2). The GRCAE proof follows Euler-Lagrange conditions for the intrinsic Dirichlet penalty; the GDAE proof expands in normal coordinates and then transforms back to a local chart.

anchors.section: C.2-C.3 GDAE conditions and theorem proof

key_findings.claim: The geometric formulation substantially improves controlled score estimation as intrinsic dimension grows, but the best geometric estimator depends on the manifold and task.
key_findings.evidence: On SPD-matrix mixtures, GRCAE is usually best or statistically comparable and geometric methods avoid the severe high-dimensional errors of Euclidean DAE/RCAE/LSLDG. On hyperspheres, GDAE and GRCAE similarly dominate at n=6 and n=10, while R-LSLDG is competitive in the smallest case.

key_findings.claim: The downstream evidence is broad but mixed and often uses favorable task-specific selection information.
key_findings.evidence: GDAE has the best autoencoder MMD on spherical sampling but S-Flow wins three of four datasets; it clearly improves Newsgroup clustering, yet DAE beats it on COIL-20 and the difference is weak on ETH-80. Sampling selects step size by validation MMD, covariance clustering selects corruption noise by validation labels, and synthetic filtering selects iteration controls against clean targets.

key_findings.claim: Some applications are useful approximations to the geometric framework, not exact implementations of the theorem.
key_findings.evidence: The point-cloud experiment diagonalizes the Fisher metric, replaces exponential-map corruption by x + sqrt(G^-1) epsilon, and uses a modified Chamfer loss rather than geodesic distance; the authors explicitly say this no longer perfectly matches the GDAE definition. The normal-distribution experiment also separates and locally approximates the mean and covariance geometry.

key_findings.claim: Exact geometric contraction becomes computationally prohibitive well before the tested denoising approximation does.
key_findings.evidence: For S^100, a GRCAE update takes 1,100 ms versus 6.15 ms for an AE; for P(14), GRCAE takes 28,776 ms versus 3.73 ms. The reported full score experiment at P(4) takes 116,255 seconds for GRCAE, versus 33 seconds for LSLDG and 545 seconds for R-LSLDG.

key_findings.claim: The real DTI demonstration does not establish clinical denoising validity.
key_findings.evidence: It uses one randomly selected healthy ADNI subject, has no ground-truth clean tensor field, reports only qualitative axial-slice comparisons, and explicitly calls for radiologist concordance to ensure that anatomy is not erased as noise.

method.core_idea: Define reconstruction, corruption, and contraction using intrinsic Riemannian operations so the regularized autoencoder learns a coordinate-independent score field on structured data.
method.mechanism: A network maps a manifold back to itself. GDAE perturbs an input by tangent Gaussian noise followed by the exponential map and minimizes geodesic reconstruction error. GRCAE adds the harmonic-map Dirichlet energy. At small noise, the metric-weighted reconstruction residual estimates the derivative of the log density and can drive Langevin sampling, mean-shift clustering, or iterative filtering.
assumptions: The data space is a smooth Riemannian manifold and its metric and required geometric operators are known or accurately approximated.
The corruption scale is small enough for the O(sigma^2) expansion and local-chart arguments to be accurate.
The reconstruction map, metric, density, and required higher derivatives are smooth and bounded.
Training finds a solution close enough to the population first-order optimum for the residual to represent the score.
Metric, geodesic, exponential-map, and Jacobian approximations preserve the task-relevant geometry.

techniques.role: Creates isotropic manifold corruption by sampling a tangent Gaussian and applying the exponential map.
Makes reconstruction error intrinsic to the known data manifold.
Generalizes contractive regularization through coordinate-invariant Dirichlet energy.
Converts the small-noise reconstruction displacement into a manifold log-density gradient.
Uses the learned geometric score for Riemannian Langevin sampling.
Makes point-cloud and SPD applications tractable through diagonal, Taylor, and split-geometry approximations.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic mixtures on SPD matrices P(n) and hyperspheres S^n.
evaluations.metric: Mean metric-weighted squared error of the estimated geometric score over five runs.
evaluations.result: GDAE/GRCAE outperform Euclidean variants strongly at higher dimensions; GRCAE is often best but is much slower.

evaluations.metric: MMD between test points and Riemannian-Langevin samples.
evaluations.result: GDAE is the best autoencoder on every row, but the purpose-built S-Flow has lower MMD on three of four datasets.
evaluations.baseline: DAE, RCAE, GRCAE, and spherical normalizing flow.

evaluations.setting: Newsgroup20 spherical document embeddings and ETH/COIL SPD image descriptors.
evaluations.metric: Adjusted Rand index over five runs.
evaluations.result: GDAE wins Newsgroup tasks and COIL-100, is tied on ETH-80, and loses to DAE on COIL-20.
evaluations.baseline: Euclidean and ambient DAE/LSLDG plus R-LSLDG.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic N(2) tensor-field denoising and one real ADNI DTI scan.
evaluations.metric: Synthetic R-squared and qualitative real-scan visualization.
evaluations.result: GDAE improves synthetic filtering except MVKR is slightly better at the largest noise; the real scan has no quantitative or clinical ground truth.

evaluations.setting: ShapeNet-to-ModelNet point-cloud transfer under four noise levels.
evaluations.result: GDAE is increasingly better than AE/DAE as noise grows; combining it with isometry regularization is usually strongest.
evaluations.baseline: AE, DAE, and an isometry-regularized AE.

limitations: The score identity is a population, small-noise asymptotic result rather than a finite-sample or optimization-error guarantee.
Most applications require a known metric and usable exponential, logarithm, distance, or eigendecomposition routines.
Multiple-chart networks and learned unknown metrics are proposals, not evaluated systems.
GRCAE Jacobian regularization is orders of magnitude slower at the larger tested dimensions.
Several hyperparameters are selected with labels, clean targets, ground-truth score surrogates, or validation MMD that may not exist in deployment.
The real medical example lacks clean targets, multiple subjects, quantitative outcomes, and expert validation.
The point-cloud implementation breaks exact correspondence with the stated GDAE objective.
failure_modes: A coordinate chart crosses a singularity or boundary and the local residual no longer represents a stable intrinsic displacement.
Noise is too large for the local expansion or too small to produce a learnable denoising signal.
Approximated metrics, distances, or exponential maps distort the actual manifold score.
GRCAE Jacobian computation exhausts memory or compute as intrinsic dimension grows.
Iterated reconstruction collapses distinct modes or removes medically meaningful structure as if it were noise.
A score model trained only near observed samples behaves arbitrarily along an MCMC trajectory outside that region.
Validation leakage makes a tuned downstream result look more transferable than it is.
reusable_insights: Geometry-aware learning should replace each non-invariant pipeline operation, not merely constrain the output layer.
A denoising residual can be a reusable score estimator when its noise law and reconstruction metric share the same geometry.
Exact intrinsic objectives and their tractable approximations should be named and evaluated separately.
Coordinate-frame perturbation is a direct invariance test and should be standard for manifold models.
Downstream mode-seeking requires off-support score accuracy, which should be measured independently from reconstruction on training points.
Matched runtime and memory curves matter because geometric Jacobians can reverse an apparent accuracy advantage.
open_questions: Can finite-sample score error be bounded after approximate geometry and incomplete optimization are included?
Can Hutchinson estimators, tangent low-rank structure, or implicit differentiation make geometric contraction competitive with denoising?
How should corruption scale be selected without access to ground-truth scores, clean targets, or downstream labels?
Which metric approximations preserve sampling and clustering behavior rather than only reconstruction error?
Can atlas-overlap consistency be enforced for learned multi-chart reconstruction maps?
Does expert-blinded DTI validation show that iterative mode seeking removes artifacts without deleting anatomy?

competitive_landscape.title: Riemannian Score-Based Generative Modelling
competitive_landscape.difference: De Bortoli et al. learn a time-dependent score for a forward diffusion and reverse it to generate manifold data; this paper recovers one small-noise score from an autoencoder and reuses it for several non-generative tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: Riemannian Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Huang et al. derive likelihood training and Riemannian score matching for continuous-time diffusion on arbitrary manifolds; the reviewed work instead gives an autoencoder residual identity and no likelihood objective.

competitive_landscape.title: Flow Matching on General Geometries
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen and Lipman regress a manifold vector field without score simulation or divergence computation on simple geometries and handle meshes; the autoencoder route is simpler conceptually but its exact contraction and geometric operators scale poorly.

competitive_landscape.title: Geometry-Aware Generative Autoencoders for Warped Riemannian Metric Learning and Generative Modeling on Data Manifolds
competitive_landscape.difference: GAGA learns a warped metric from on- and off-manifold samples for generation and trajectories, addressing unknown geometry; the reviewed method assumes or hand-approximates a task metric and targets denoising-score recovery.

competitive_landscape.title: Score-based pullback Riemannian geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: Diepeveen et al. use a learned density to define pullback geometry with closed-form maps and an autoencoder dimension-error bound; the reviewed method goes in the opposite direction, using a supplied geometry to learn the density score.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Coordinate-invariant denoising and reconstruction-contractive autoencoders preserve the classical reconstruction-residual score identity for non-Euclidean data and support diverse downstream uses.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper supplies an intrinsic objective, local small-noise derivations for both variants, manifold-specific implementations, and experiments spanning scores, sampling, clustering, tensor filtering, and point-cloud transfer.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The unified geometric replacement of reconstruction, noise, and contraction is a substantive contribution. Its strongest exact claim is asymptotic and assumes known smooth geometry; several practical wins rely on approximations and favorable selection, while subsequent manifold diffusion and flow-matching methods offer stronger generative machinery and better scaling.

reviewer_notes: Read all 35 pages, including the invariance and score proofs, manifold-specific implementations, runtime tables, every experimental appendix, and rendered main-paper figures and tables. The complete corresponding-author copy matches the accepted ICLR 2023 paper. Competing work was checked against primary arXiv, ICLR, and PMLR records on 2026-08-23.
